BENCHMARK EXECUTION CONTRACT

Run identity / isolation
- Model: `ox-alpha`.
- All project files must live under `C:\Users\Epic\Documents\ChatGPT\Ox model test`.
- Required folder: `<Project Name> [model:ox-alpha] [<harness-key>] [run:<NN>]`.
- Use a short lowercase harness key. Start at `run:01`; if that project/model/harness already exists, atomically claim the next available two-digit run number.
- Never overwrite, reuse, rename over, or modify another run's folder. Keep project dependencies/artifacts inside this run folder where practical.

Browser-only + parallel testing
- Finished project must run in a standard modern browser. Local dev servers are fine; Electron/Tauri/native runtimes are not substitutes.
- Assume many runs test simultaneously. Use a unique free localhost port, isolated browser profile/context, and run-scoped temp/cache/download/trace/screenshot artifacts.
- Never hijack, navigate, close, or kill unrelated browser tabs/processes/servers, and never kill something merely to free a port.
- Track/clean up only resources created by this run. Prefer headless testing unless visible interaction is genuinely required.

- Keep critical runtime assets/dependencies local or bundled when practical so the finished project does not unnecessarily depend on fragile third-party CDNs/APIs just to boot.
- Handle browser user-gesture restrictions correctly for features such as audio, fullscreen, pointer lock, clipboard, autoplay, or similar browser-gated capabilities; provide a clear user action instead of silently failing.
- If the project has non-obvious controls or shortcuts, expose them clearly in the experience through a controls/help overlay, onboarding hint, pause/menu screen, or similarly discoverable UI.

Execution efficiency
- Prefer the shortest direct implementation path that satisfies the task; investigate only enough to unblock building.
- Batch related checks when practical. Use bounded retries and switch strategy when an approach repeatedly fails.
- Preserve working progress. Finish the core vertical slice before extras.
- Avoid scope creep, prolonged architecture archaeology, over-debugging non-blockers, and stalling on optional services/assets; use sensible local/generated/mock fallbacks when useful.
- Verify real functionality, but do not run huge regression/stress/profiling suites unless a discovered issue warrants them.

Quality + performance
- Build a polished, coherent finished experience, not a checklist demo.
- Prioritize usability, visual quality, interaction feel, responsive feedback, consistent styling, and sensible design decisions.
- Avoid unfinished/debug/placeholder-looking final states when better treatment materially improves the result.
- Implement important behavior for real rather than faking it for screenshots. Keep code organized without overengineering.
- Keep runtime smooth/resource-conscious: avoid unbounded objects/effects/listeners/workers/requests, unnecessary per-frame work, runaway CPU/GPU/memory use, oversized assets, and performance that degrades over time.
- Reuse/pool/batch/cull/pause/clean up work when useful. Optimize the actual experience, not synthetic numbers, and do not sacrifice meaningful quality just to chase metrics.

Optional capabilities
- You may use any additional input modalities, inspection capabilities, or environment-provided tools when genuinely useful. Their use is optional; do not create extra work simply because they exist.

OPTIONAL CAPABILITY — ISOLATED E2E TESTING (contested-machine browser protocol)
If this run does any browser automation / E2E testing / screenshots and
{{E2E_ISOLATION_SKILL_PATH}} is not UNAVAILABLE, read and follow that SKILL.md
before your first browser/playwright step. Core rules it enforces: prefer
deterministic non-browser tests; ONE tab maximum (a second client is a raw
in-page WebSocket or node script, never a second tab); stamp every tab
(window.__TID) and re-assert stamp+URL before EVERY browser tool call;
abandon silently any tab showing someone else's page; keep trigger→assert
steps atomic under UI fade/expiry windows; clean up only process PIDs you
recorded spawning — never name-filter sweeps. Skill artifacts stay inside
this run's project folder. If the path is UNAVAILABLE, proceed using the
isolation rules above.

IMAGE GENERATION — USE THIS SKILL, NOTHING ELSE
If image generation/editing would genuinely help, use only:
`C:\Users\Epic\.agents\skills\gpt-image-2\scripts\gpt_image.mjs`
No API keys or browser automation for image generation.

Rules:
- Node 18+; always pass `-o`; parse stdout exactly.
- Do not wrap/parallelize the script or create sleep-loop retry logic; keep `--delay-ms >= 1500`.
- Plus capacity is limited (~50 images/3h), so wait instead of retry-spamming limits.
- On 401, tell the user to run `codex login`.
- Sizes: `1024x1024|1024x1536|1536x1024`; quality: `low|medium|high`.

Single:
`node "C:\Users\Epic\.agents\skills\gpt-image-2\scripts\gpt_image.mjs" -o out.png "PROMPT"`
Successful stdout = exactly one line, the absolute PNG path.

Batch:
`node "C:\Users\Epic\.agents\skills\gpt-image-2\scripts\gpt_image.mjs" --n 10 --quality low -o sheet.png "PROMPT"`
Outputs `sheet-1.png`...`sheet-10.png`; exit `0` all ok / `2` partial / `1` fail; logs on stderr.

Edit:
`node "C:\Users\Epic\.agents\skills\gpt-image-2\scripts\gpt_image.mjs" --ref input.png -o out.png "INSTRUCTION"`

For >3 images/background work:
`node "C:\Users\Epic\.agents\skills\gpt-image-2\scripts\gpt_image.mjs" queue add [-o x.png] "PROMPT"`
`node "C:\Users\Epic\.agents\skills\gpt-image-2\scripts\gpt_image.mjs" queue run --detach`
`node "C:\Users\Epic\.agents\skills\gpt-image-2\scripts\gpt_image.mjs" queue status --json`
Poll about every 20s until `pending==0 && running==0`.
Use `queue list --json` for `.path`/`.error`; retry failed items with `queue run --retry-failed`.

CONDITIONAL MULTIPLAYER BUILD CONTRACT v2
Applies only if multiplayer is included. Epic handles deployment; you build only.
- Produce ONE self-contained static build folder suitable for `OxAlpha/<Project>/<Harness>/`.
- Do NOT deploy, push, SSH, edit compose files, touch Traefik, or run anything on the server.

  `{"title":"<Human Name>","description":"<one line>","multiplayer":{"endpoint":"/ws/<project-slug>"}}`
- Slug must be lowercase `[a-z0-9-]` and match the `server.mjs` route exactly.

Optional backend:
- If needed, add ONE `server.mjs` beside entry: ESM, Node builtins only, no npm packages, no `listen()`, no spawned server.
- Platform loads a default export with optional `maxSockets`, optional `tickMs`, and `create(ctx)` returning `open`, `message`, `close`, optional `tick`, optional `stop`.
- `ws` provides `{ id, send(obj|string), close(code), query(URLSearchParams), ip }`.
- State is memory-only; clients reconnect/rejoin after restart. Keep handlers deterministic/fast. If offline-only, omit `server.mjs`.

Client netcode:
- Same-origin/subpath-safe only:
  `const url=(location.protocol==="https:"?"wss://":"ws://")+location.host+"/ws/<project-slug>";`
- Never hardcode domains/ports/`ws://localhost` or root-absolute asset/worker/importScripts paths.
- Auto-reconnect with backoff and graceful disconnected UI.
- Netcode belongs in normal source dirs.
- Game must still boot pure-static if backend is down, and from `file://` or a dumb static server.

Multiplayer handoff: state Project, Harness, entry path, endpoint, and message protocol/event payloads.

FINAL VERIFICATION / HANDOFF
- Launch the real project in a browser and exercise the core experience enough to catch obvious blockers.
- Screenshots are mandatory. Capture real running states inside this run's project folder, inspect them yourself, and fix obvious broken/blank/loading/unusable visuals.

Create concise `RESULT.md` with:
Project; Model `ox-alpha`; Harness; Run; Status (completed/partial/failed); launch instructions; screenshot paths; major known issues; duration/turn count if exposed.

A normal README + `RESULT.md` is sufficient unless the project genuinely needs more documentation.

The journal OBSERVES the active local agent/session system.

THE JOURNAL NEVER CONTROLS THE AGENT RUNNER.

CURRENT RUNNER ONLY
==================================================

Observe only the local agent/session system associated with the CURRENT execution environment.

Do NOT spend significant implementation time building integrations for unrelated runners.

==================================================

Do not assume unrelated agent runners are relevant to this workflow.

Do NOT recursively search the computer trying to discover every possible coding-agent installation.

Focus specifically on the installed agent-runner environment.

If evidence indicates that some session/state belongs to another runner:

IGNORE IT.

Do not ingest it into the agent journal.

==================================================
PRIMARY USER-FACING AGENT SESSIONS ONLY
==================================================

THIS IS A HARD REQUIREMENT.

ONLY inspect primary user-facing sessions.

Do NOT indiscriminately ingest:

- subagent sessions;
- delegated-agent sessions;
- worker sessions;
- temporary execution contexts;
- internal system sessions;
- background agent contexts;

- unrelated agent histories.

==================================================

Determine how the agent runner stores or exposes:

- primary user-facing sessions;
- messages;
- user messages;
- assistant messages;
- timestamps;
- goals;
- tool events;
- session IDs;
- session types;
- parent/child relationships;
- running/completed state;
- process/activity state.

==================================================
VERIFY THAT A SOURCE ACTUALLY BELONGS TO THE CURRENT RUNNER
==================================================

Before ingesting any session file/database/directory:

VERIFY that it belongs to the current runner.

Do not assume something belongs to the current runner merely because:

- it contains JSON;
- it contains chat messages;
- it looks agent-related;
- it was recently modified.

Use strong evidence such as:

- the current runner's installation paths;
- agent-runner configuration;
- runner-specific metadata;
- a known runner/session schema;
- application identifiers;
- documented runner/session storage behavior;
- other reliable local evidence.

If a source cannot be confidently identified as belonging to the current runner:

DO NOT INGEST IT.

==================================================
DETERMINE PRIMARY SESSION IDENTITY
==================================================

Determine how primary user-facing sessions can reliably be distinguished from:

- subagents;
- delegated sessions;
- child sessions;
- workers;
- temporary sessions;
- background/internal sessions.

Use the current runner's actual metadata/schema/relationships.

Do NOT guess.

Implement deterministic filtering.

Add tests for this filtering.

==================================================
ABSOLUTE READ-ONLY REQUIREMENT
==================================================

The journal is an OBSERVER.

It is NOT an agent controller.

It MUST NEVER:

- send a message to the agent runner;
- inject a prompt;
- create an agent session;
- continue a session;
- resume a session;
- pause a session;
- stop a session;
- cancel a session;

- reject an action;
- modify agent-runner history;
- modify agent state;
- modify agent-runner databases;
- kill the agent runner;
- restart the agent runner;
- alter agent-runner configuration;
- obtain disruptive/exclusive locks;
- otherwise influence an active session.

If the agent is currently working:

LEAVE IT ALONE.

READ STATE ONLY.

==================================================
SAFE READING OF ACTIVE STATE
==================================================

The agent runner may be writing session state while the journal reads it.

Design accordingly.

Use techniques such as:

- read-only database access;
- safe snapshots;
- tolerant parsing;
- bounded retries;
- incremental reads;
- atomic journal writes.

Do not obtain exclusive locks that could interfere with the agent runner.

If the newest record is partially written:

DO NOT CRASH.

Ignore/retry it during the next lightweight refresh.

==================================================
USER PROMPTS — PRIMARY ARCHIVE
==================================================

I specifically want to see:

THE PROMPT OR PROMPTS I SENT TO THE AGENT.

For every primary user-facing session, preserve my user messages accurately where legitimately accessible.

This includes:

- initial instructions;
- long task prompts;
- ordinary follow-up messages;
- corrections;
- additional requirements;
- short prompts;
- later modifications to the task.

Do NOT assume every important instruction uses a special command prefix.

The initial user message establishes the initial request.

Subsequent user messages may modify or extend it.

Preserve them chronologically.

==================================================
PROMPT DISPLAY
==================================================

The website should directly display MY prompts.

Conceptually:

Build... 


FOLLOW-UP

[1:31 PM]

Make sure the game...


FOLLOW-UP

[2:16 PM]

Also test...


Long prompts should support:

EXPAND / COLLAPSE

so the page remains readable.

Provide a useful:

COPY PROMPT

action if practical.

==================================================
DO NOT DISPLAY RAW MODEL RESPONSES
==================================================

I DO NOT want the agent's full responses shown in the journal.

Do NOT build a transcript viewer containing:

USER
ASSISTANT
USER
ASSISTANT

Do NOT display giant agent responses.

Do NOT expose raw chain-of-thought/internal reasoning.

Do NOT expose hidden/internal model state.

agent responses have ONE purpose here:

STATUS EVIDENCE.

==================================================
RECENT AGENT RESPONSES MAY BE READ INTERNALLY
==================================================

The status engine MAY read a SMALL, BOUNDED amount of recent agent output from primary user-facing sessions.

This is necessary to determine things such as:

- what the agent is currently doing;
- recent progress;
- current phase;
- tests being executed;
- blockers;
- failures;
- whether implementation appears complete;
- whether the session appears to still be running.

Example:

INITIAL USER PROMPT:

Anime Gacha RPG

STATUS
RUNNING

The raw agent prose should generally NOT be displayed.

==================================================
RECENT MEANS RECENT
==================================================

Do NOT repeatedly parse an entire very long agent run merely to determine:

"currently running tests."

Use:

INITIAL USER PROMPT
+
SUBSEQUENT USER PROMPTS
+
RECENT RELEVANT AGENT EVENTS/MESSAGES
+
CURRENT SESSION STATE.

Read only enough recent agent context to determine state.

Make the recent-context/event limit configurable.

Use incremental checkpoints.

Do not continuously reprocess ancient assistant messages.

==================================================
LIVE SESSION STATUS
==================================================

The website should provide a prominent:

ACTIVE NOW

section when primary user-facing sessions are active.

For each active session show useful information such as:

PROJECT / TASK

RUNNER / ENVIRONMENT
<Current Runner>

STATUS

CURRENT ACTIVITY

CURRENT PHASE

LAST ACTIVITY

RECENT PROGRESS

BLOCKER

STATUS CONFIDENCE.

Example:

3D Anime Gacha RPG

<Current Runner>

● RUNNING

Current activity:
Building first playable 3D character.

Current phase:
3D asset implementation

Recent progress:
✓ Visual bible created
✓ GPT Image 2 concepts generated
● Character model implementation underway

Last activity:
1 minute ago

Blocker:
None detected

==================================================
STATUS MODEL
==================================================

Create a coherent status model.

Potential statuses:

QUEUED
RUNNING
IMPLEMENTING
TESTING
BLOCKED
WAITING
COMPLETED
FAILED
STOPPED
UNKNOWN

Choose/refine the final set based on actual agent state semantics.

Do not mark something COMPLETED simply because my prompt asked the agent to complete it.

==================================================
STATUS CONFIDENCE
==================================================

Where useful distinguish:

DIRECTLY OBSERVED

INFERRED

UNKNOWN.

Example:

SESSION RUNNING
Directly observed.

CURRENT TASK:
"Testing summon flow"
Inferred from recent agent state.

This prevents the dashboard from presenting guesses as certainty.

==================================================
LIVE STATUS REFRESH
==================================================

The five-hour archival update should NOT be responsible for live status.

Implement a separate lightweight READ-ONLY live observer.

Use an appropriate refresh interval such as:

tens of seconds

or

a few minutes.

Choose something lightweight enough to have negligible impact.

Prefer:

check session metadata/state
→ detect meaningful change
→ read new relevant events
→ update status.

DO NOT invoke an AI model every 30 seconds just to summarize status.

Do NOT recursively scan huge directories every 30 seconds.

Use incremental/change-driven techniques.

==================================================
PROMPT VS REPORTED VS VERIFIED
==================================================

The journal MUST distinguish THREE concepts.

1. REQUESTED

What I asked the agent to do.

2. REPORTED / OBSERVED AGENT PROGRESS

What recent agent state indicates it did or is currently doing.

3. VERIFIED ACTIVITY

What independent evidence such as:

- files;
- Git;
- tests;
- builds;
- generated artifacts;
- project state

supports as actually having happened.

Do not collapse these into one thing.

==================================================
DO NOT TRUST PROMPTS AS PROOF
==================================================

If my prompt says:

"Build Minecraft"

that proves:

REQUESTED:
Build Minecraft.

It does NOT prove:

COMPLETED:
Minecraft built successfully.

Use additional evidence.

Likewise:

The agent saying:

"tests pass"

is useful reported evidence.

But if accessible test/build artifacts independently confirm it, mark that as stronger VERIFIED evidence.

==================================================
PROJECT DISCOVERY
==================================================

Inspect relevant development locations, especially:

C:\Users\Epic\Documents\ChatGPT\Ox model test

and other project locations directly referenced by primary-session prompts where safe and appropriate.

Do not blindly crawl my entire filesystem.

Discover project activity through evidence such as:

- project directories;
- source changes;
- Git repositories;
- Git commits;
- tests;
- builds;
- generated assets;
- project metadata;
- timestamps.

==================================================
DAILY ACTIVITY
==================================================

For each day, determine what actually happened.

Create concise factual summaries.

Example:

MINECRAFT

Requested:
Browser Minecraft recreation.

Status:
Completed / In Progress / etc.

Verified activity:
- voxel world implementation changed;
- terrain system added;
- headless tests executed.

Prompts:
3

Last activity:
4:38 PM

Do not fabricate accomplishments.

==================================================
CALENDAR — MAJOR UI FEATURE
==================================================

Build a real calendar interface.

The calendar should make the journal easy to navigate historically.

When the site starts:

AUTO-SELECT THE CURRENT DAY.

If today contains data:

IMMEDIATELY DISPLAY TODAY'S JOURNAL.

Do not make me click today's date every time.

==================================================
CALENDAR DAY INDICATORS
==================================================

Dates containing activity should be visually distinguishable.

Potential indicators may communicate:

- activity exists;
- number of projects;
- completed projects;
- active sessions;
- particularly busy days.

Keep it readable.

Do not turn the calendar into visual noise.

==================================================
CLICKING A DAY
==================================================

The day view should contain useful sections such as:

DAILY SUMMARY

PROMPTS SENT

TODAY

action.

==================================================

==================================================

==================================================

==================================================

Terrain generation implemented

Headless gameplay test

12:03:01 running
12:03:31 running
12:04:01 running

etc.

Deduplicate insignificant status noise.

==================================================
FIVE-HOUR HISTORICAL UPDATE
==================================================

Approximately every:

5 HOURS

perform a larger historical reconciliation pass.

This pass should examine new activity since the last successful checkpoint.

Conceptually:

LAST CHECKPOINT
→ NEW USER PROMPTS
→ RECENT AGENT STATE
→ FILESYSTEM ACTIVITY
→ GIT ACTIVITY
→ TEST/BUILD EVIDENCE
→ RECONCILE
→ UPDATE JOURNAL
→ SAVE CHECKPOINT.

==================================================
NO DUPLICATES
==================================================

The five-hour updater MUST be idempotent.

Running it repeatedly over overlapping time ranges should NOT create duplicate:

- prompts;
- projects;
- events;
- commits;
- statuses;
- accomplishments.

Design stable identifiers/deduplication.

==================================================
DOWNTIME / CATCH-UP
==================================================

The PC may:

- sleep;
- restart;
- shut down;
- have the journal manually stopped.

Persist the last successful historical checkpoint.

Example:

Last successful scan:
1:00 AM

PC sleeps.

Journal starts:
10:00 AM

The next update should inspect:

1:00 AM → 10:00 AM.

Do NOT permanently lose the missing period.

4. discover current primary user-facing sessions;
5. initialize live status;

==================================================

THIS APPLICATION MUST BE LIGHTWEIGHT.

Do not create another resource monster merely to report what the other resource monsters are doing.

- repeated complete-history parsing;
- unnecessary model calls;
- heavyweight polling;
- endless browser automation;
- runaway databases;
- enormous duplicated archives.

- timestamps;
- hashes/IDs;
- checkpoints;
- filesystem metadata;
- bounded context;
- efficient database queries;
- change detection.

==================================================

==================================================

Choose an appropriate solution such as:

SQLite

if suitable.

Design a coherent schema for things such as:

DAYS

PROJECTS

SESSIONS

USER PROMPTS

STATUS EVENTS

VERIFIED ACTIVITIES

GIT EVENTS

BLOCKERS

CHECKPOINTS.

Use migrations/versioning where appropriate.

Do not store everything as one enormous fragile JSON blob unless there is a strong reason.

Minecraft
GPU-P

etc.

Black-screen investigation

Aug 23
Remote deployment

Do not force project history to exist only inside individual calendar days.

==================================================
DASHBOARD / TODAY VIEW
==================================================

Today's page should feel especially useful.

Consider sections such as:

ACTIVE NOW

TODAY'S PROJECTS

PROMPTS SENT TODAY

COMPLETED TODAY

BLOCKED

RECENT ACTIVITY

TIMELINE.

Use actual data.

==================================================
DESIGN
==================================================

Make this look like a polished developer/AI operations journal.

It should feel:

- modern;
- technical;
- information-dense;
- premium;
- fast;
- readable.

Do NOT create a generic SaaS landing page.

This is an application I may leave open while agents work.

Prioritize information hierarchy.

==================================================
RESPONSIVE DESIGN
==================================================

The journal should work well on:

- large desktop;
- laptop;
- tablet;
- phone.

==================================================
LOCALHOST / PORT SAFETY
==================================================

Many Ox goals/projects may be running simultaneously.

==================================================
PRIVACY
==================================================

This journal may contain my development prompts.

Treat it as private local data.

Do NOT:

- expose it publicly;
- upload the database;
- send prompts to unrelated services;
- publish session data;
- publish secrets.

==================================================

==================================================

==================================================
DESKTOP CONTROL FOLDER
==================================================

Create a dedicated folder on my Windows Desktop:

Daily Ship Log Controls

powershell.exe
chrome.exe
chromium.exe

or other unrelated processes.

or another safe ownership mechanism.

RUNNING

RUNNING

session observer:
RUNNING

9:12 PM

OPEN should NOT start a duplicate backend.

If the service is stopped, either:

or

- safely start it first if that produces the better UX.

Choose and document the behavior.

==================================================
OPTIONAL AUTO-START
==================================================

Design the application so Windows startup auto-launch can be enabled later easily.

Do NOT automatically create invasive startup behavior unless clearly appropriate.

Document how to enable it.

==================================================
HEADLESS DEVELOPMENT + TESTING
==================================================

All AUTOMATED browser testing must remain headless.

Do NOT take control of my active browser.

Do NOT:

- move my cursor;
- steal focus;
- type on my desktop;
- close unrelated applications.

Use isolated headless browser automation.

==================================================
VISUAL QA
==================================================

Capture screenshots headlessly.

ACTUALLY INSPECT THEM.

Test approximately:

1920x1080
1440x900
1366x768
1024x768
768x1024
390x844
360x800

Inspect:

- calendar;
- today view;
- active sessions;
- project cards;
- prompt display;
- long agent prompts;

- search;

- status badges;

Fix visual defects.

==================================================
FUNCTIONAL TESTING
==================================================

Build automated tests covering:

- session-source verification;
- primary-session filtering;
- rejection of subagent sessions;
- user-message extraction;
- assistant-response exclusion from display;
- bounded recent-agent-state reading;

- empty days;
- search;

==================================================
READ-ONLY SESSION TEST
==================================================

Explicitly verify that observing an active primary user-facing session does NOT modify it.

Where safely measurable:

record relevant agent session metadata/state

→ perform observer reads

The observer should have ZERO write path into the current runner.

==================================================
SIMULATED SESSION TESTS
==================================================

==================================================

simulated downtime

new activity during gap

==================================================
FIVE-HOUR UPDATE TEST
==================================================

Test the scheduler using controlled/mock time where appropriate.

Verify:

==================================================
ITERATION
==================================================

Do not accept the first implementation merely because it runs.

Use it against actual primary user-facing sessions READ-ONLY.

Look at the site.

Test it.

Find confusing states.

Improve them.

If the calendar sucks:

improve it.

If prompt browsing sucks:

improve it.

If status inference is noisy:

improve it.

If the observer consumes too many resources:

optimize it.

If primary-session detection is unreliable:

fix it.

If STOP could kill unrelated processes:

fix it before completion.

==================================================
DEFINITION OF DONE
==================================================

The goal is complete only when:

- the project exists in the correct Ox model-test directory;
- the current runner/session source has been verified;
- relevant skills were inspected;
- the current runner's real local session architecture was investigated;

- automated browser testing was headless;

==================================================
FINAL REPORT
==================================================

When complete, report:

1. run identifier;
2. exact project directory;
3. Desktop control directory;
4. localhost URL;
5. technology stack;
6. agent installation/session source discovered;

Do not claim information was verified when it was merely inferred.

Do not display raw agent responses merely because you read them for status.

Do not interrupt my running agent sessions.

Do not stop at a plan.

BUILD IT.
RUN IT.
POINT IT AT THE REAL PRIMARY USER-FACING AGENT SESSIONS READ-ONLY.

I WANT TO OPEN A DATE MONTHS FROM NOW AND SEE EXACTLY WHAT THE HELL WE COOKED THAT DAY. 🔥

BENCHMARK EXECUTION CONTRACT

Run identity / isolation
- Model: `ox-alpha`.
- All project files must live under `C:\Users\Epic\Documents\ChatGPT\Ox model test`.
- Required folder: `<Project Name> [model:ox-alpha] [<harness-key>] [run:<NN>]`.
- Use a short lowercase harness key. Start at `run:01`; if that project/model/harness already exists, atomically claim the next available two-digit run number.
- Never overwrite, reuse, rename over, or modify another run's folder. Keep project dependencies/artifacts inside this run folder where practical.

Browser-only + parallel testing
- Finished project must run in a standard modern browser. Local dev servers are fine; Electron/Tauri/native runtimes are not substitutes.
- Assume many runs test simultaneously. Use a unique free localhost port, isolated browser profile/context, and run-scoped temp/cache/download/trace/screenshot artifacts.
- Never hijack, navigate, close, or kill unrelated browser tabs/processes/servers, and never kill something merely to free a port.
- Track/clean up only resources created by this run. Prefer headless testing unless visible interaction is genuinely required.

- Keep critical runtime assets/dependencies local or bundled when practical so the finished project does not unnecessarily depend on fragile third-party CDNs/APIs just to boot.
- Handle browser user-gesture restrictions correctly for features such as audio, fullscreen, pointer lock, clipboard, autoplay, or similar browser-gated capabilities; provide a clear user action instead of silently failing.
- If the project has non-obvious controls or shortcuts, expose them clearly in the experience through a controls/help overlay, onboarding hint, pause/menu screen, or similarly discoverable UI.

Execution efficiency
- Prefer the shortest direct implementation path that satisfies the task; investigate only enough to unblock building.
- Batch related checks when practical. Use bounded retries and switch strategy when an approach repeatedly fails.
- Preserve working progress. Finish the core vertical slice before extras.
- Avoid scope creep, prolonged architecture archaeology, over-debugging non-blockers, and stalling on optional services/assets; use sensible local/generated/mock fallbacks when useful.
- Verify real functionality, but do not run huge regression/stress/profiling suites unless a discovered issue warrants them.

Quality + performance
- Build a polished, coherent finished experience, not a checklist demo.
- Prioritize usability, visual quality, interaction feel, responsive feedback, consistent styling, and sensible design decisions.
- Avoid unfinished/debug/placeholder-looking final states when better treatment materially improves the result.
- Implement important behavior for real rather than faking it for screenshots. Keep code organized without overengineering.
- Keep runtime smooth/resource-conscious: avoid unbounded objects/effects/listeners/workers/requests, unnecessary per-frame work, runaway CPU/GPU/memory use, oversized assets, and performance that degrades over time.
- Reuse/pool/batch/cull/pause/clean up work when useful. Optimize the actual experience, not synthetic numbers, and do not sacrifice meaningful quality just to chase metrics.

Optional capabilities
- You may use any additional input modalities, inspection capabilities, or environment-provided tools when genuinely useful. Their use is optional; do not create extra work simply because they exist.

OPTIONAL CAPABILITY — ISOLATED E2E TESTING (contested-machine browser protocol)
If this run does any browser automation / E2E testing / screenshots and
{{E2E_ISOLATION_SKILL_PATH}} is not UNAVAILABLE, read and follow that SKILL.md
before your first browser/playwright step. Core rules it enforces: prefer
deterministic non-browser tests; ONE tab maximum (a second client is a raw
in-page WebSocket or node script, never a second tab); stamp every tab
(window.__TID) and re-assert stamp+URL before EVERY browser tool call;
abandon silently any tab showing someone else's page; keep trigger→assert
steps atomic under UI fade/expiry windows; clean up only process PIDs you
recorded spawning — never name-filter sweeps. Skill artifacts stay inside
this run's project folder. If the path is UNAVAILABLE, proceed using the
isolation rules above.

IMAGE GENERATION — USE THIS SKILL, NOTHING ELSE
If image generation/editing would genuinely help, use only:
`C:\Users\Epic\.agents\skills\gpt-image-2\scripts\gpt_image.mjs`
No API keys or browser automation for image generation.

Rules:
- Node 18+; always pass `-o`; parse stdout exactly.
- Do not wrap/parallelize the script or create sleep-loop retry logic; keep `--delay-ms >= 1500`.
- Plus capacity is limited (~50 images/3h), so wait instead of retry-spamming limits.
- On 401, tell the user to run `codex login`.
- Sizes: `1024x1024|1024x1536|1536x1024`; quality: `low|medium|high`.

Single:
`node "C:\Users\Epic\.agents\skills\gpt-image-2\scripts\gpt_image.mjs" -o out.png "PROMPT"`
Successful stdout = exactly one line, the absolute PNG path.

Batch:
`node "C:\Users\Epic\.agents\skills\gpt-image-2\scripts\gpt_image.mjs" --n 10 --quality low -o sheet.png "PROMPT"`
Outputs `sheet-1.png`...`sheet-10.png`; exit `0` all ok / `2` partial / `1` fail; logs on stderr.

Edit:
`node "C:\Users\Epic\.agents\skills\gpt-image-2\scripts\gpt_image.mjs" --ref input.png -o out.png "INSTRUCTION"`

For >3 images/background work:
`node "C:\Users\Epic\.agents\skills\gpt-image-2\scripts\gpt_image.mjs" queue add [-o x.png] "PROMPT"`
`node "C:\Users\Epic\.agents\skills\gpt-image-2\scripts\gpt_image.mjs" queue run --detach`
`node "C:\Users\Epic\.agents\skills\gpt-image-2\scripts\gpt_image.mjs" queue status --json`
Poll about every 20s until `pending==0 && running==0`.
Use `queue list --json` for `.path`/`.error`; retry failed items with `queue run --retry-failed`.

CONDITIONAL MULTIPLAYER BUILD CONTRACT v2
Applies only if multiplayer is included. Epic handles deployment; you build only.
- Produce ONE self-contained static build folder suitable for `OxAlpha/<Project>/<Harness>/`.
- Do NOT deploy, push, SSH, edit compose files, touch Traefik, or run anything on the server.
- Multiplayer build folder: `<Project>-<Harness>` (Hermes harness unless told otherwise).
- Entry: root `index.html`, or `public/index.html` with that structure intact.
- `arcade.json` beside entry:
  `{"title":"<Human Name>","description":"<one line>","multiplayer":{"endpoint":"/ws/<project-slug>"}}`
- Slug must be lowercase `[a-z0-9-]` and match the `server.mjs` route exactly.

Optional backend:
- If needed, add ONE `server.mjs` beside entry: ESM, Node builtins only, no npm packages, no `listen()`, no spawned server.
- Platform loads a default export with optional `maxSockets`, optional `tickMs`, and `create(ctx)` returning `open`, `message`, `close`, optional `tick`, optional `stop`.
- `ws` provides `{ id, send(obj|string), close(code), query(URLSearchParams), ip }`.
- State is memory-only; clients reconnect/rejoin after restart. Keep handlers deterministic/fast. If offline-only, omit `server.mjs`.

Client netcode:
- Same-origin/subpath-safe only:
  `const url=(location.protocol==="https:"?"wss://":"ws://")+location.host+"/ws/<project-slug>";`
- Never hardcode domains/ports/`ws://localhost` or root-absolute asset/worker/importScripts paths.
- Auto-reconnect with backoff and graceful disconnected UI.
- Netcode belongs in normal source dirs.
- Game must still boot pure-static if backend is down, and from `file://` or a dumb static server.

Multiplayer handoff: state Project, Harness, entry path, endpoint, and message protocol/event payloads.

FINAL VERIFICATION / HANDOFF
- Launch the real project in a browser and exercise the core experience enough to catch obvious blockers.
- Screenshots are mandatory. Capture real running states inside this run's project folder, inspect them yourself, and fix obvious broken/blank/loading/unusable visuals.
- Screenshots must show the actual result, not merely an editor, terminal, loading screen, or blank browser.
- Fix obvious stutter, major loading/resource issues, degraded-over-time performance, broken interactions, and major usability problems encountered during normal use.
- Do not claim completion if the core experience is broken.

Create concise `RESULT.md` with:
Project; Model `ox-alpha`; Harness; Run; Status (completed/partial/failed); launch instructions; screenshot paths; major known issues; duration/turn count if exposed.

A normal README + `RESULT.md` is sufficient unless the project genuinely needs more documentation.

IMPORTANT DESIGN CLARIFICATION:

I want this game to be a FULL 3D ANIME GACHA ACTION RPG.

Do NOT make the primary game:

- 2D;
- 2.5D;
- a card battler;
- a visual novel;
- an isometric game;
- a menu-driven gacha simulator;
- a collection of 2D screens with occasional gameplay.

The actual playable world MUST be 3D.

==================================================
3D GAME REQUIREMENT
==================================================

Build:

- 3D anime-style playable characters;
- 3D environments;
- 3D exploration;

- opponent and player note sections;
- health tug-of-war;
- score;
- combo;
- misses;
- accuracy;
- judgment feedback;
- pause/restart;
- win and fail states.

Create from scratch a short, polished, ORIGINAL browser-based **first-person horror game** that I can finish in roughly one sitting. Focus on atmosphere, exploration, a few interconnected puzzles, and at least one genuine threat/chase sequence.

Do not make a direct clone of an existing horror franchise. Do not spoil every scare in the opening instructions or UI.

# PLAYER

# PUZZLES

Include roughly 3–4 understandable interconnected objectives/puzzles. Favor observation, environment manipulation, codes, item use, power routing, spatial reasoning, or similar interactions over arbitrary guessing.

# HORROR / THREAT

Use lighting, sound, pacing, environmental changes, and uncertainty to build tension.

Include at least one real threat sequence: chase, stalking enemy, timed escape, or another mechanic where the player can genuinely fail. It should be possible to understand what went wrong and retry without restarting the entire game.

# AUDIO / VISUALS

Use a cohesive visual style that performs well in-browser and supports the atmosphere.

# VERIFY

# DEFINITION OF DONE

I should be able to play a complete short horror experience with atmosphere, meaningful exploration, solvable puzzles, at least one actual danger sequence, and a real ending. It should feel authored and tense, not like a randomly dark hallway demo.

Create from scratch an original browser-based **3D factory/tycoon game** where I physically walk around, place production machines, connect a simple production chain, earn money, automate it, and expand.

Think compact spatial factory game / Roblox-tycoon energy, NOT an idle-game webpage full of upgrade buttons.

START SMALL → PLACE MACHINES → PRODUCE ITEMS → MOVE/PROCESS THEM → SELL OUTPUT → EARN MONEY → UPGRADE/AUTOMATE → EXPAND.

Create a small 3D factory plot with responsive character or free-camera movement. Make placement spatial and visible in the world.

Implement a contained set of production pieces such as:
- resource producer/extractor;
- conveyor;
- processor/refiner;
- assembler;
- storage;
- seller/output station.

Start with limited funds and a tiny production option. Selling output should finance better machines, speed/capacity upgrades, additional plot space, or more valuable recipes.

Balance the first progression arc so meaningful upgrades happen during a normal test session rather than after hours of idle waiting.

Use satisfying machine animations, moving products, sounds, status lights, income feedback, and clear placement previews. The factory should visibly become busier as it grows.

Persist progress locally. Before handoff, start from a fresh save, build a working production chain, produce and sell items, purchase at least one meaningful upgrade/expansion, confirm automation continues, save/reload, and verify the factory state returns. Screenshots should show both an early and developed factory state if practical.

# DEFINITION OF DONE

I should be able to walk around my plot, build a real visible production line, watch items move through machines, make money, reinvest it, automate more of the factory, save, reload, and keep expanding. It must feel like a spatial factory game, not a spreadsheet with a 3D background.

PROJECT BRIEF

Build a browser-based multiplayer team shooter focused on objective modes.

Core experience:
- Support approximately 4v4 or 5v5 players.
- Use one compact, well-designed arena that works across multiple modes.
- Include at least:
  1. Capture the Flag
  2. Team Deathmatch
  3. King of the Hill / Control Point
- Optionally add a domination-style multi-zone mode if it fits naturally without bloating scope.
- Include team assignment, respawning, round timer, score limits, scoreboard, match-end flow, and rematch/map-mode restart.
- Provide several distinct weapon types with readable roles, such as rifle, shotgun, burst weapon, projectile weapon, or another balanced mix.
- Movement and shooting should feel responsive and satisfying in-browser.
- Synchronize player movement, health/death, shots or hit results, weapon state, objectives, scoring, respawns, and match state robustly.
- Use server authority where appropriate for critical shared state while keeping local input responsive.
- Include clear team colors/readability, objective markers, hit/damage feedback, ammo/reload state, and spawn protection or safe spawning.
- Prevent obvious duplicate flag captures, impossible objective ownership, duplicated kills, or other simple race-condition bugs.
- Include a lobby/ready flow and graceful handling for disconnects.
- Keep the arena and weapon roster contained enough to polish properly.

This is the heaviest multiplayer benchmark in this batch. Prioritize solid netcode, responsive combat, clear objective play, and one excellent arena over content quantity.
